     1	NAME
     2	podman-volume-create - Create a new volume
     3	SYNOPSIS
     4	podman volume create [options] [name]
     5	DESCRIPTION
     6	Creates an empty volume and prepares it to be used by containers. The volume
     7	can be created with a specific name, if a name is not given a random name is
     8	generated. You can add metadata to the volume by using the --label flag and
     9	driver options can be set using the --opt flag.
    10	OPTIONS
    11	--driver, -d=driver
    12	Specify the volume driver name (default local).
    13	There are two drivers supported by Podman itself: local and image.
    14	The local driver uses a directory on disk as the backend by default, but can also use the mount(8) command to mount a filesystem as the volume if --opt is specified.
    15	The image driver uses an image as the backing store of for the volume.
    16	An overlay filesystem is created, which allows changes to the volume to be committed as a new layer on top of the image.
    17	Using a value other than local or image, Podman attempts to create the volume using a volume plugin with the given name.
    18	Such plugins must be defined in the volume_plugins section of the containers.conf(5) configuration file.
    19	--gid=gid
    20	Set the GID that the volume will be created as. Differently than --opt o=gid=*gid*, the specified value is not passed to the mount operation. The specified GID will own the volume’s mount point directory and affects the volume chown operation.
    21	--help
    22	Print usage statement
    23	--ignore
    24	Don’t fail if the named volume already exists, instead just print the name. Note that the new options are not applied to the existing volume.
    25	--label, -l=label
    26	Set metadata for the volume (e.g., --label mykey=value). Can be used multiple times.
    27	These labels can be viewed in podman volume inspect or podman volume ls.
    28	--opt, -o=option
    29	Set driver specific options.
    30	For the default driver, local, this allows a volume to be configured to mount a filesystem on the host.
    31	For the local driver the following options are supported: type, device, o, and [no]copy.
    32	The type option sets the type of the filesystem to be mounted, and is equivalent to the -t flag to mount(8).
    33	The device option sets the device to be mounted, and is equivalent to the device argument to mount(8).
    34	The copy option enables copying files from the container image path where the mount is created to the newly created volume on the first run. copy is the default.
    35	The o option sets options for the mount, and is equivalent to the filesystem
    36	options (also -o) passed to mount(8) with the following exceptions:
    37	The o option supports uid and gid options to set the UID and GID of the created volume that are not normally supported by mount(8).
    38	The o option supports the size option to set the maximum size of the created volume, the inodes option to set the maximum number of inodes for the volume, and noquota to completely disable quota support even for tracking of disk usage.
    39	The size option is supported on the “tmpfs” and “xfs[note]” file systems.
    40	The inodes option is supported on the “xfs[note]” file systems.
    41	Note: xfs filesystems must be mounted with the prjquota flag described in the xfs_quota(8) man page. Podman will throw an error if they’re not.
    42	The o option supports using volume options other than the UID/GID options with the local driver and requires root privileges.
    43	The o options supports the timeout option which allows users to set a driver specific timeout in seconds before volume creation fails. For example, --opt=o=timeout=10 sets a driver timeout of 10 seconds.
    44	Note Do not confuse the --opt,-o create option with the -o mount option. For example, with podman volume create, use -o=o=uid=1000 not -o=uid=1000.
    45	For the image driver, the only supported option is image, which specifies the image the volume is based on.
    46	This option is mandatory when using the image driver.
    47	When not using the local and image drivers, the given options are passed directly to the volume plugin. In this case, supported options are dictated by the plugin in question, not Podman.
    48	--uid=uid
    49	Set the UID that the volume will be created as. Differently than --opt o=uid=*uid*, the specified value is not passed to the mount operation. The specified UID will own the volume’s mount point directory and affects the volume chown operation.
    50	QUOTAS
    51	podman volume create uses XFS project quota controls for controlling the size and the number of inodes of builtin volumes. The directory used to store the volumes must be an XFS file system and be mounted with the pquota option.
    52	Example /etc/fstab entry:
    53	/dev/podman/podman-var /var xfs defaults,x-systemd.device-timeout=0,pquota 1 2
    54	Podman generates project IDs for each builtin volume, but these project IDs need to be unique for the XFS file system. These project IDs by default are generated randomly, with a potential for overlap with other quotas on the same file
    55	system.
    56	The xfs_quota tool can be used to assign a project ID to the storage driver directory, e.g.:
    57	echo 100000:/var/lib/containers/storage/overlay >> /etc/projects
    58	echo 200000:/var/lib/containers/storage/volumes >> /etc/projects
    59	echo storage:100000 >> /etc/projid
    60	echo volumes:200000 >> /etc/projid
    61	xfs_quota -x -c 'project -s storage volumes' /<xfs mount point>
    62	In the example above we are configuring the overlay storage driver for newly
    63	created containers as well as volumes to use project IDs with a start offset.
    64	All containers are assigned larger project IDs (e.g. >= 100000).
    65	All volume assigned project IDs larger project IDs starting with 200000.
    66	This prevents xfs_quota management conflicts with containers/storage.

    68	Create empty volume.
    69	$ podman volume create
    70	Create empty named volume.
    71	$ podman volume create myvol
    72	Create empty named volume with specified label.
    73	$ podman volume create --label foo=bar myvol

     3	SYNOPSIS

     5	DESCRIPTION
     6	Remove unused volumes. By default only anonymous (unnamed) unused volumes are removed.
     7	Anonymous volumes are those created with a container (e.g. podman run -v /path without a volume name).

    14	--all can be combined with --filter: --all widens the set of candidate volumes to all unused ones, and the filters then restrict which of those are removed. For example, --all --filter label!=keep removes every unused volume that does not have the keep label.
    15	--dry-run

    17	--filter
